script: I complimented her photo—then I was caught in a nightmare.. The client's office smelled like stale coffee and old books. I hadn't met him before, but the big‑name account was on my desk, and senior management had insisted I be the one to handle it, even though I hadn't closed a deal in five years. (Why the hell would they pick a rookie over a seasoned pro who actually knows how to make money? I am better at this than they are.) The meeting went fine. We signed papers, I tucked the folder into my briefcase, and I was about to head out when I spotted a framed photo on his desk. The brain‑bug that's always on my case flipped on. "Aww, what a lovely picture, is that you and your father?" I blurted out. He stared at me like I'd just spoken in the wrong language. "That's my wife," he said, voice sharp enough to cut glass. I froze, then slipped into a robotic apology that sounded like a posh detective from a 1960s film. "Right-oh, very good." (I'd never used that phrase before today.) The small talk dead‑ended. I muttered a weak "thanks for having me," grabbed my files, and fled the room. Now I am hunting for a way to hand this account over to someone else. (Honestly, I think this is the last time he's going to give us business.)
